4.chapter: Scanning Laser Polarimetry (GDx VCC & ECC): Microtubule Birefringence, Corneal Compensation & NFI
4.quote: GDx measures phase retardation of 780 nm polarized light passing through birefringent axonal microtubules, proportional to RNFL thickness. VCC uses macular Henle fibers to cancel corneal birefringence, ECC suppresses atypical birefringence patterns (ABPs), and NFI (>50 abnormal) offers optimal discrimination.

mcqs.q: In the Heidelberg Retina Tomograph (HRT), where is the standard reference plane automatically positioned to separate the neuroretinal rim (above) from the optic cup (below)?
options: At the level of Bruch's membrane opening (BMO)
150 µm posterior to the anterior lamina cribrosa surface
50 µm posterior to the mean retinal surface height along the temporal papillomacular bundle (350°–356°) on the contour line
At the internal limiting membrane peak of the superior arcuate bundle
mcqs.explanation: HRT sets its standard reference plane 50 µm posterior to the mean surface height along the temporal papillomacular bundle (350°–356°), assuming this region remains relatively stable until advanced glaucoma.

mcqs.q: How does GDx with Variable Corneal Compensation (GDx VCC) determine and neutralize an individual patient's anterior segment (corneal) birefringence before measuring peripapillary RNFL retardation?
options: By measuring the radially symmetric 'bow-tie' retardation pattern of the macular Henle fiber layer
By performing Scheimpflug corneal pachymetry and subtracting central corneal thickness
By applying a Fourier transform to an 840 nm spectral interferogram
By scanning 64 confocal Z-axis planes through the corneal stroma
mcqs.explanation: GDx VCC images the macula first; because the radially oriented Henle fibers act as a uniform radial retarder, any superimposed non-uniform 'bow-tie' retardation reflects corneal/lenticular birefringence, which the variable retarder then cancels.

mcqs.q: In a patient with advanced POAG (visual field MD −18 dB) whose circumpapillary RNFL average thickness on SD-OCT has plateaued at 49 µm across consecutive visits, why may further structural glaucomatous loss fail to register on cpRNFL thickness?
options: Corneal birefringence cancels out RNFL reflectivity below 50 µm
Non-neural glial cells, blood vessels, and connective tissue create an asymptotic OCT 'measurement floor' around 45–55 µm
SD-OCT axial resolution is limited to 300 µm in advanced optic atrophy
Posterior vitreous detachment artificially prevents macular GCIPL thinning
mcqs.explanation: Even after complete RGC axonal loss, residual glial tissue and retinal blood vessels prevent cpRNFL thickness on OCT from dropping below an asymptotic floor (~45–55 µm); macular GCIPL and central 10-2 visual fields remain more sensitive for monitoring advanced progression.

cards.label: OCT Generations & Optics
cards.front: Compare Time-Domain, Spectral-Domain, and Swept-Source OCT by optical mechanism, wavelength, scan speed, and axial resolution.
cards.back: All apply **low-coherence (Michelson) interferometry** • **TD-OCT:** Oscillating reference mirror, ~840 nm, **~400 A-scans/s**, **~10 µm** resolution • **SD-OCT (Cirrus/Spectralis):** Stationary mirror + spectrometer + **inverse Fourier transform**, **~840 nm**, **27,000–100,000 A-scans/s**, **3–5 µm** axial resolution (EDI-OCT images deep lamina cribrosa/choroid) • **SS-OCT:** Tunable **~1050 nm** laser, **100,000–200,000+ A-scans/s**, wide-field disc+macula cubes & deeper penetration.

cards.label: cpRNFL, BMO-MRW & GCIPL
cards.front: Define circumpapillary RNFL, BMO-MRW, and macular GCIPL/GCC on OCT, and explain why macular GCIPL excels in high myopia and advanced glaucoma.
cards.back: **cpRNFL:** Measured on a **3.4–3.46 mm circle** (normal **~90–105 µm**, aging −0.2 to −0.5 µm/yr; **TSNIT double-hump**); inferotemporal/superotemporal thinning is most sensitive early • **BMO-MRW:** Shortest distance from **Bruch's membrane opening to ILM** over 360° (eliminates tilted/myopic disc-margin ambiguity) • **Macular GCIPL/GCC:** Captures **~50% of RGCs**, avoids myopic PPA/tilt artifacts, and **tracks progression after cpRNFL hits its ~45–55 µm floor**.

cards.label: HRT Optical & Analysis Tools
cards.front: Describe the optical principle of the Heidelberg Retina Tomograph (HRT) and distinguish MRA, GPS, Cup Shape Measure (CSM), and TCA.
cards.back: **Principle:** **670 nm** confocal scanning laser ophthalmoscopy with pinhole rejecting scatter across **32–64 Z-sections** (axial resolution **~300 µm**, surface topography only) • **MRA:** Compares disc-size-adjusted rim area (manual Elschnig contour line; WNL / Borderline 95–99.9% / ONL >99.9%) • **GPS:** Automated **contour-independent** 3D model • **CSM:** Normally negative; shifts toward 0/positive with glaucomatous sloping • **TCA:** Event-based 4×4 superpixel height depression.

cards.label: GDx Birefringence, ECC & NFI
cards.front: What physical property does GDx measure, how does GDx ECC improve on VCC, and what are the diagnostic Nerve Fiber Indicator (NFI) cutoffs?
cards.back: **Principle:** **780–785 nm** polarimetry measures **phase retardation** from **form birefringence of parallel RGC axonal microtubules** (~0.67 nm/µm RNFL; detects early microtubule loss) • **ECC vs. VCC:** ECC adds a known bias retarder (later subtracted) to boost SNR and suppress **atypical birefringence patterns (ABPs)** in myopes/light fundi • **NFI (0–100 SVM):** **<30 normal**, **31–50 borderline**, **>50 likely glaucoma** (confounded by LASIK/scars/maculopathy).
